title: Approximation of Analytic Functions by ReLU Neural Networks with Adjustable Depth and Width
summary: In contrast to most studies on neural network approximation theory that characterize results through a single parameter, such as the total number of network parameters, \cite{shen2020deep} pioneered the characterization of approximation rates as a joint function of the width parameter $N$ and the depth parameter $L$, thereby granting greater architectural flexibility. Existing works using the $(N,L)$-characterization focus on function classes with finite smoothness $s$, establishing a typical approximation rate of $\mathcal{O}\left(N^{-2s/d}L^{-2s/d}\right)$ with $d$ denoting the input…
